Watch one run of /modernize

/modernize reads a collection. You run the read-only script collect-mysql.sql on your own database, and it writes the workload's statements, tables and counters into one JSON file. It may read table rows to measure value sizes, but no row values go into the file. Statements arrive as digests with their values replaced, alongside your schema and routine code, and you can read the script before you run it.

This is a real run on the WordPress sample, recorded in a terminal. Scroll down to play it and scroll up to rewind. When the run ends, keep scrolling to see the results it produced.

    Run it yourself

    1. Clone the repository and unzip docs/examples/wordpress/wordpress.zip in its folder.
    2. Open Claude Code in the repository.
    3. Type /modernize docs/examples/wordpress/wordpress-collection.json. The run stops at the gate for your approval. Add --auto to skip the question.

    The replay is a terminal recording of one run, sampled into text frames as you scroll. Home paths, session identifiers and the session details in the status line are blanked, and the recording ends a few seconds after the result line. Every figure in the captions comes from that run's own reports or from the recording.
